output.text: The robotics workshop filled the school gym with tables of gears, wires, and small motors. Assume that Gus is the lead volunteer. Gus arrived early to help set up the registration table near the entrance. Ben came in wearing a bright green jacket and immediately found a seat near the soldering station. Rosa arrived a few minutes after Ben, chatting with one of the younger students about her favorite robot design. Quinn showed up carrying a backpack full of spare parts collected from a previous competition. Uma brought the first-aid kit. Gus is taller than Quinn, though Rosa is taller than both of them. Ben and Rosa worked different shifts. Throughout the morning, the students rotated between stations to test their circuits and calibrate their sensors. Rosa and Quinn worked different shifts. Uma is younger than Gus but older than Ben, according to the sign-in sheet. The mentors circulated the room, offering tips on wiring and balance for the walking robots. Ben and Quinn worked different shifts. Someone had labeled every worktable with a number so that materials would not get mixed up. The shop ran three shifts. By the end of the day, most of the robots could move across the floor without tipping over, and a few even avoided obstacles using simple sensors. The students compared notes about which battery packs lasted longest, and several teams promised to bring improved designs to the next session. Everyone helped stack the folding chairs before the doors were locked for the evening.
